rubrics.justification: The response overcalls the image as a favorable full/early-full blastocyst with identifiable good TE and a likely compact ICM, whereas the image appears more collapsed/poorly expanded with indistinct ICM and non-crisp TE. It relies heavily on the provided Gardner score rather than the visible morphology.

It integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, diagnosis, semen parameters, endometrium, and first-cycle status well, and appropriately notes that low oocyte yield affects future cycle planning more than this embryo's intrinsic quality.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with a logical link from young age and favorable clinical context to a moderate-good prognosis. Minor weakness is that the prognosis is partly built on an optimistic morphology interpretation despite the image being less convincing.

Recommendations are broadly evidence-based: single embryo transfer, standard luteal support, avoidance of unsupported add-ons, and not overreacting after one failed transfer. Minor issue is some imprecision around day-4 blastocyst grading/interpretation.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support, activity guidance, and future cycle review. Useful clinically, though somewhat generic and not highly tailored to the discrepancy between image appearance and reported grade.
